Real Madrid: “Something is happening, watch out!” – Thierry Henry impressed by Mourinho's emerging side

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 09:50.
  • Real Madrid thrashed PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday night and are growing in strength this season, thanks to the work of Jose Mourinho and the form of several players.
  • Thierry Henry's words on CBS on Tuesday night sum up the feeling that is starting to emerge around Real Madrid:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 09:50.

Real Madrid thrashed PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday night and are growing in strength this season, thanks to the work of Jose Mourinho and the form of several players.

Thierry Henry's words on CBS on Tuesday night sum up the feeling that is starting to emerge around Real Madrid:.

It has been revealed that 'Real Madrid played an exceptional game. Playing like that, they are serious contenders for the Champions League. They are improving enormously from week to week. Something is going on at Real Madrid, watch out!'.

After a start to the season marked by some turbulence, Real Madrid appear to have found their cruising speed. The spectacular win over PSV Eindhoven (5-1) in the Champions League confirmed that impression. Mourinho's side have just strung together a tenth consecutive victory in all competitions and have a perfect record in the Champions League, with five wins from five games. Above all, Real Madrid seem to have taken a step forward in their ability to turn games around.

It has been revealed that the script against the Dutch side was far from straightforward. Trailing at half-time after a particularly worrying first half, Real Madrid looked a completely different team after the break. It was a reaction that bore the signature of their manager, who made three changes at half-time.

Sources indicate that the other big positive of the evening was Jude Bellingham. Left on the bench at kick-off, the Englishman made a sensational entrance at half-time, to the point of transforming his side. His work rate, ability to get forward and influence between the lines immediately gave Real Madrid more options. His superb goal, scored after a remarkable piece of skill, rewarded a top-class performance.

Thierry Henry, again, was full of admiration:.

Sources indicate that '(Jude) Bellingham is incredible, the way he plays. Wearing the number 5 at Real Madrid is not easy, but he does it with astonishing ease. His personality is extraordinary. I cannot believe that some people doubted him in his own country. But he has silenced the sceptics with his current performances and proved to them that they were wrong at the World Cup. He always delivers with his attitude and his play.'.

It has been revealed that beyond his statistics, with seven goals and five assists in 18 appearances, Bellingham brings an extra dimension to Real Madrid's midfield. Mourinho therefore has a player capable of turning a game, but also of giving a real identity to the side's attacking play.

Industry observers note that the Englishman's performance should not, however, overshadow Mourinho's decisions. At half-time, the Portuguese made a bold call with three changes: Bellingham, Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen replaced Aurelien Tchouameni, Antonio Rudiger and Eder Militao. It was a spectacular reshuffle, particularly at centre-back, where the two starters were punished after a difficult first half.

But there was also a desire to rebalance the side behind this choice. By installing Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva in midfield, Mourinho prioritised technical control and ball circulation. Real Madrid were able to push their block up, press higher and regain control of the game. The manager also explained that he used several video clips during the break to correct his players' defensive and attacking mistakes.

According to Jamie Carragher on CBS:.

'Mourinho is building a fantastic team. Week after week, we see them improving. They lost to Atletico Madrid and we thought the season was over, but they managed to pull themselves together by beating Barcelona' - Carragher stated.

The former Liverpool player's comments reflect an enthusiasm that now goes beyond the result of a single match. With a manager capable of changing the course of a game, a rediscovered Bellingham and a side gaining in coherence, Real Madrid are starting to look like credible contenders for the European title. At the same time, Paris Saint-Germain have lost two attacking options in Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Report – West Ham prepared to cut their losses on January exit that suits all parties

💡 Key Takeaways
  • From the sound of it, West Ham United are going all-in to refresh their options in front of goal in January.
  • Neither Pablo Felipe nor Taty Castellanos have fulfilled the expectations that were present when they were signed in the January window at the start of this year – Taty especially was expected to boss the Championship after the Hammers were relegated but at times he’s appeared no more than a scowling misfit, unable to influence games when he’s been called upon.
  • Footballinsider.com – who are usually on the ball with their reporting – have it apparently on good authority that West Ham are prepared to sanction his departure in January even though the club will have to absorb yet another huge financial hit:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From the sound of it, West Ham United are going all-in to refresh their options in front of goal in January. The club face a crisis with none of their trio of goal scorers looking fit for purpose: The best of the three, Joel Piroe, has amassed four goals this season whilst the other two have managed just one goal apiece.

Neither Pablo Felipe nor Taty Castellanos have fulfilled the expectations that were present when they were signed in the January window at the start of this year – Taty especially was expected to boss the Championship after the Hammers were relegated but at times he’s appeared no more than a scowling misfit, unable to influence games when he’s been called upon.

‘What a waste of money” as the song goes….

Footballinsider.com – who are usually on the ball with their reporting – have it apparently on good authority that West Ham are prepared to sanction his departure in January even though the club will have to absorb yet another huge financial hit:.

“Sources: West Ham to accept Taty Castellanos loss ahead of January”.

Runs their article, detailing West Ham’s willingness to sell the forward, despite being fully aware that they’ll not see anything like the £26 million they paid for the Argentine striker just twelve months ago:.

“The 28-year-old has scored just one goal from 15 games in the Championship this season, and is performing way below the level West Ham expected from him.

Sources say that the East London outfit are prepared to sell Castellanos at a loss this winter, knowing that it will be “very difficult” to recoup the £26million they paid for him.”.

Recent findings suggest that this is the key: Taty had previously been linked with loan moves back to Argentina which were never really feasible. The fact that West Ham are apparently putting it ‘out there’ that they’ll take the hit in order to move the striker on means that bids should be forthcoming in the winter market from a number of clubs; several who’ll no doubt chance their arm hoping to get him for a bit of a steal.

One goal in 15 games in the second division is nothing to write home about though, and so West Ham’s approach is borne largely out of facing the undeniable fact that Castellanos has been a massive disappointment, not to mention a colossal waste of money.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.

Since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium. The Greek attacker scored 17 goals and made 23 assists in 36 league games.

In a recent development, but doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League. In his first stint in England with Norwich City, he indicated little sign of becoming the player he is now.

Since making his debut for the club, Tzolis has become a more rounded attacking threat. He has started all 7 Premier League games this season and provides a reliable option on the left for Arteta.

However, in recent comments, it seems that he is aware of the perceptions around his physicality and is keen to change them.

Tzolis spoke to Arsenal Media, saying that he doesn’t think the notion of him lacking the physicality to play at top level has validity.

Industry observers note that he claimed that he is not a player without muscle and cited his accomplishments. He also described his tendency to use aggression against his opponents.

It has been revealed that this is a key part of Arteta’s system at the club. Tzolis is expected to press from the flanks if Arsenal lose the ball.

Tzolis is comfortable with this role. He is able to track back well to support his full-back, adding an extra dimension to the left side.

In a recent development, the Greek international has proven his physical ability outside of match play. He was nicknamed Leonidas by the fitness team at the club due to a strong performance in pre-season.

It is reported that he completed the running challenge better than anyone in the squad.

Recent findings suggest that tzolis has joined Arsenal to add attacking flair to the squad, having left for Besiktas. He looks like he could be a formidable goalscorer and creator.

In the league last season, Tzolis contributed 40 goals and put in a good performance in Europe. This led to Arsenal spending a reported £34 million to bring him to the club.

He has not had the best impact in the league, registering just one assist and no goals, but this should not be taken to mean he is not contributing.

Tzolis has shown an ability to fit into Arteta’s style of play. His defensive contribution, work rate and combative nature may prove very valuable in tough away games.

Despite there being plenty to improve on, Tzolis provides more than just an attacking option for Arsenal.

If Tzolis can change people’s view of him in terms of his physicality and continues to put his technical skills and determination together, then he can be a valuable asset in Arteta’s prepares.

Potential signings of Alex Scott and Nico Paz may pose a challenge for Arteta.

While both players would add quality to the squad, their arrival would be a consideration for current players in the Emirates squad.

Sources indicate that scott would add quality in midfield, and Paz adds creativity and versatility going forward. Arteta must consider that adding these players may hinder the development of current players.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on bringing Alex Scott to the club.

After rejecting contract offers from Bournemouth, Scott could only have one year left on his contract at the club next summer. However, he is understood to be valued by Bournemouth at over £100m.

He would be a great addition for Arteta, with the versatility and skill he has. He could give added competition in midfield.

Yet his potential arrival raises questions about Myles Lewis-Skelly’s future role.

In a recent development, myles Lewis-Skelly was included in the Champions League final line-up last season. He highlighted that he is trusted by the club.He has also demonstrated his commitment by remaining at the club despite opportunities to gain regular playing time at other clubs.

Nico Paz presents another interesting option for Arsenal.

Paz joined Como from Real Madrid in the summer. He has caught the eye of a number of substantial clubs and has increased his appeal with strong performances in international football. The 22-year-old has scored 5 times in his last 5 games for Argentina.

Paz is a versatile right-sided player and could be an appealing addition to Arteta’s strike force.

There are already plenty of players fighting for attacking positions at Arsenal.

Bukayo Saka is key in the team’s attack, and with Martin Ødegaard and Noni Madueke in the squad too, there are plenty of options. Max Dowman is a young player looking to break into the first team.

Sources indicate that although Arsenal are facing challenges in attracting quality players to the club. They now also face issues in managing a squad with experienced internationals and developing young players.

Although Scott and Paz would improve the depth of the squad, players must not be sacrificed for fresh players if they have already shown quality.

It has been revealed that players such as Lewis-Skelly and Dowman may be negatively affected by this. Opportunities may be taken away from them if the club continues to spend large amounts of money on upcoming players.

However, it is still very important for Arsenal to bring in quality players to compete for major titles.

Know how the additions will integrate within the playing style and how they affect the other players within the squad.

According to recent reports, the Gunners can strengthen further without overloading the squad. Good additions can be made to the first XI whilst also providing a realistic chance for young players to come through from within the academy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Dowman shortly returns to action for Arsenal after serving a three-game suspension.

According to recent reports, his absence has been disappointing, but the experience should give the youngster an crucial lesson. Can he put the incident behind him and show Mikel Arteta that he can be trusted?

In a recent development, dowman received a red card against Fleetwood Town after kicking out at Harrison Neal. Arsenal appealed the decision, but the FA rejected the club’s appeal.

The suspension ruled him out of three domestic fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle United.

It has been revealed that he’ll be back on 29 November as Arsenal take on Manchester City. This should give the young star a chance to get his season back on track and showcase what makes him such a highly-rated player.

Industry observers note that dowman looks very promising for the future. He has shown great adaptability playing with the more experienced players and has the self-belief to make an impact in games.

He has performed well in the Carabao Cup. In the 4-2 win against Ipswich, Dowman scored two goals, showing his flair and poise in front of goal.

Arteta has given him opportunities to play in the Premier League and Champions League, meaning that he appears to have a clear route into the first team.

Although Dowman still has a lot to learn, he displays great potential in his technical ability and combative nature. As he gets more games under his belt, fans will be excited to see how he progresses.

Dowman was sent off in an unfortunate moment. He was heavily challenged by Neal and, after lashing out, was shown a straight red card.

Although this one moment should not be enough to dismiss a young player from the game completely, it can serve as a valuable lesson on the pressure that comes with playing at a higher level.

Recent findings suggest that opponents will test Dowman physically, but he must learn to keep his composure. As he starts making an impact, some players may target his age and inexperience to unsettle him.

As he gets more game time, consistency will be key. Arteta must be confident that Dowman can be relied on in high pressure situations.

It has been revealed that arsenal do not need to rush Dowman into the first team. The squad’s quality allows Arteta to manage his minutes and give him time to develop without putting too much pressure on him.

If Dowman is to play against Manchester City, it will depend on Arteta’s looks, but he has certainly done enough to warrant consideration.

According to recent reports, the suspension should not define his season. What matters now is how he responds, both on and off the pitch.

Dowman has the talent to become an notable player for Arsenal. Keeping his discipline will be just as important as displaying his ability.

Tech Report: Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.
  • It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game.
  • Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Industry observers note that matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Recent findings suggest that matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager stated. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

Recent findings suggest that the win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the fresh arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

According to recent reports, even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

It has been revealed that ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV.

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

Recent findings suggest that it was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Recent findings suggest that nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Sources indicate that when Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

Industry observers note that so Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline states. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Recent findings suggest that today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

According to recent reports, frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

David Moyes’ record-breaking night as Everton manager could not have been more miserable.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record for most games in the dugout.

But that was about the only positive he could take away from the Gtech Community Stadium, as high-flying Brentford battered ten-man Everton on an evening to forget for the 63-year-old Scotsman.

Daily Mail Sport's Bobby Manzi was at the Gtech Community Stadium on a torrid night for the Toffees...

The Bees can mix it with massive boys.

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again.

They climbed to sixth, leapfrogging Leeds — who have had far more praise lavished on them this season than Keith Andrews’ reliable side.

Brentford are disciplined with plenty of attacking flair, even with frontman and top goalscorer Igor Thiago suspended.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record.

‘We set out this season looking to be better than last season, and if that happens, we will be flying to different destinations next season,’ Andrews said of their European hopes.’.

In a recent development, ‘We've got a very competitive squad that strives to get better. If we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place.

‘I enjoyed us,’ he added about the performance. ‘I thought we were very good. We played with real bravery, courage and energy.’.

James Tarkowski endured a depressing return to his former club when he was shown the first Premier League red card of his career.

However, they were ultimately given a bit of a humbling by Milan, who won 5-1 thanks to a ruthless counter-attacking display.

Some have questioned if the Canarini were a bit too aggressive in their approach to the game, given they played with such a high line and allowed space for Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to exploit.

Alvini was present in the press conference room at San Siro after the full-time whistle and he analysed what was perhaps the most difficult night of the season for his team. MilanNews transcribed his assessments.

Should the game have been played differently?

In a recent development, “Frosinone played their game but made a few mistakes they don’t usually make, but that’s certainly not my concern, losing by such a large margin. What’s worrying are the mistakes we made that we could have avoided.”.

According to recent reports, “We made a mistake on the first goal, which was a mistake of our own, while the other goals we conceded were goals we absolutely could have avoided. We conceded them and were naive.

“It’s a mistake of our own, and so today, from this perspective, if you come to Milan against Milan and make these mistakes, it’s only natural that we end up losing like this, by such a large scoreline.

“That’s the analysis, even though I think the scoreline is even too large: the first half, in my opinion, was extraordinary on our part.”.

Did the absences have an impact, forcing you to experiment a bit?

Recent findings suggest that “There’s nothing experimental about it. We played with the same principles, running forward to get to Rabiot. We preferred to bring on a defender who would push forward rather than a midfielder.

“In my opinion, this definitely didn’t influence the result, but rather the attitude, the idea, or the match strategy. And we certainly made – as I said before and I’ll repeat – mistakes we don’t usually make.

Industry observers note that “If you give Milan certain chances, with such strong players and the quality of this team, you risk losing, and that’s what happened. You risk losing with a heavy defeat, and that’s what happened.

In a recent development, “He had a problem with that back heel in the box, and he definitely needs tests. It’s too early now; we’ll have to wait for the tests, which will be done starting Tuesday, but it’s definitely a problem.”.

“We had a chance with Monterisi after a minute, we hit the post, and we created a lot. I have nothing to say to the team for their attitude and the way they played.

“We, I repeat, made some naivety, some mistakes. It’s also up to me to understand that there are important players on the other side who can cause problems.”.

It has been revealed that “It’s a result that definitely needs to be managed, navigated, and channeled, but it doesn’t change my attitude at all. We have 20 points today. The path we need to take is to try to stay in Serie A, and we’ll try to do so with this attitude, with this identity: this is the path we’ll take.

Sources indicate that “Four years ago, I drew a game against Milan by playing defensively, and we took home a point. Today we made some mistakes, but this is the path we’ll take. I’m happier with the management, with the team’s identity, to try to achieve that objective, and this is what we’ll continue to do.”.

#129836. William D. Nordhaus obituary: economist whose tools transformed climate policy

William D. Nordhaus obituary: economist whose tools transformed climate policy

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Credit: Monica Jorge/Upcoming York Times/Redux/eyevine.
  • Sources indicate that william (Bill) Nordhaus was an economist known for introducing climate change into economic analysis, earning him the 2018 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences.
  • His research shaped our understanding of what drives economic growth and innovation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Credit: Monica Jorge/Upcoming York Times/Redux/eyevine.

Sources indicate that william (Bill) Nordhaus was an economist known for introducing climate change into economic analysis, earning him the 2018 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences. Profoundly curious and able to distill complex problems to their core, Nordhaus produced groundbreaking scholarship powered by his joy of discovery, dedication to getting things right and commitment to ensuring that science serves society.

His research shaped our understanding of what drives economic growth and innovation. He realized that omitting the environment from economic measurement would send the wrong signals about the directions of economic growth and, therefore, pioneered more-inclusive ways to measure growth.

To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.

To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.

Sources indicate that nordhaus was born in Albuquerque, Newly introduced Mexico. His father developed a ski area to the east of the city, and as a child, Nordhaus tried to derive models of snowfall. He earned an undergraduate degree in economics from Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut, in 1963, before moving to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, where he completed his PhD in 1967 under the supervision of future Nobel prizewinner Robert Solow. He then returned to Yale as an assistant professor and spent the rest of his academic career there.

Nordhaus swiftly made a name for himself by developing an early rigorous model for endogenous growth — that which occurs inside an economic system, rather than being driven by external factors. Before then, economic models had assumed that the rate of change in technology was independent of the economy.

Nordhaus’s PhD work showed that the pace of innovation depended on economic incentives, which could be altered by policy, such as through the patent system. His model also projected that research would face diminishing returns, with new ideas getting harder to find — an idea that was validated 40 years later.

Why we need an International Panel on Inequality.

Why we need an International Panel on Inequality.

Sources indicate that next, he questioned the nature of economic growth. He recalled being inspired by an article in an in-flight magazine that described gross national product (GNP) as gross national pollution. In a 1972 article titled ‘Is Growth Obsolete?’, Nordhaus and economist James Tobin wrote that GNP exaggerates economic benefits by omitting environmental damage by “treating as free things which are not really free” and that “this practice gives the wrong signals for the directions of economic growth”. GNP also understates some of the benefits of economic growth, such as increased household well-being, from inventions such as electricity and home appliances.

This work alone gave rise to three influential lines of research: climate economics, the role of national accounts in measuring sustainable development and the importance of including upcoming goods in measures of national income and economic well-being.

Nordhaus also considered the role of innovation. In a 1996 article on the history of the price of lighting, he measured the output and cost of various sources of light across human history (see go.nature.com/478rjyh). He demonstrated that the light output per unit of energy of the compact fluorescent bulb was about 30,000 times greater than that of our distant ancestors’ fire.

How countries can grow without impoverishing future generations.

Relegation, not promotion form.

“If you are going through hell, keep going” is the oft-quoted popular saying, accredited to Winston Churchill but applicable to just about any circumstance when deep in the smelly stuff.

It’s only football. We understand. But it is supposed to be the very salvation from all of the bad things going on in the world right now.

However, a sneaky peek at the ‘bookies latest odds suggest they know something we don’t, with West Ham still odds-on (3/10 this morning) to finish in the top six. I’m not a betting man but strip away the emotion (which this ‘morning after’ column is supposed to do ) and there’s still a cold, calculating expectation that someone – presumably Scott Parker – can turn this ship around. There’s still time.

West Ham are the width of a goal post away from fourth place. The season is long and it is not yet December. Get behind whichever eleven are sent out to do battle with Stoke on Saturday. And wait for the dodgy decision in our favour or the outrageous deflected goal that we don’t deserve – which will signal a change of fortunes. COYI!

Arsenal failed to improve their Champions League prospects after a disappointing 1-1 game against Borussia Dortmund in which they lost their initial lead.

According to recent reports, despite Viktor Gyökeres’ spectacular goal, Mikel Arteta’s men allowed Maximilian Beier to level just after the halftime break. Although Arsenal were presented with several good scoring opportunities, they continually lacked composure in front of goal.

Despite winning their first three league phase games, it was an expensive night for Arsenal. They have maintained their perfect record in Europe, but for just the second time in the league phase at the Emirates, the Gunners have lost points.

Arteta will also be interested to see how much effort his team expended in their pursuit of a winning goal against Manchester City on Sunday.

Arsenal began confidently and quickly forced Dortmund to defend. Noni Madueke was troublesome on the right-hand side, and although Christos Tzolis was presented with a great chance, he failed to score from a cross.

Industry observers note that just ten minutes in, Madueke played a ball into the path of Gyökeres some 25 yards out. The Swedish forward then fired a curling shot over Gregor Kobel into the net.

According to recent reports, A stunning goal from Arsenal’s forward was just what they required. Unfortunately, they were then unable to follow up this positive play.

Recent findings suggest that despite Tzolis’ effort prompting a save from Kobel, Madueke failed to score from the ball’s subsequent deflection. Likewise, Declan Rice was presented with a good opportunity when Martin Ødegaard set him up in a neat fashion.

In a recent development, despite dominating play in the first half, Arsenal made a number of poor concluding decisions. Piero Hincapié failed to score from a good position, and Gyökeres also shot high from another good play.

Dortmund did not produce much throughout the game. However, Kepa Arrizabalaga did well to save from Joane Gadou in added time.

Arsenal should have gone into half-time with a more comfortable advantage. Instead, they gave the visitors a route back into the contest.

Shortly after play resumed, Beier failed to score despite being presented with a great chance following a low cross into the six-yard area.

Recent findings suggest that despite Arsenal successfully weathering that period of pressure, Dortmund soon retaliated. Gadou broke through the middle and passed to Beier, who then rounded Gabriel before coolly beating Kepa in the 55th minute.

Arsenal then faced a tougher challenge as they sought to add a second goal against increasingly confident Dortmund.

Industry observers note that arteta brought on Eberechi Eze, and the player swiftly became involved. However, his shot was deflected just over the bar.

It has been revealed that continuing to trouble Dortmund, Madueke saw a header from Ødegaard also fly wide. A shot from Guirassy, also deflected, hit the post, and Rice then shot wide on the other side after Eze had provided an assist for him.

Despite having 29 shots at goal, the Gunners failed to make inroads. William Saliba, too, warmed up on the touchline and then did not play. Arteta continued with his existing defensive line.

Whilst Arsenal had much to be commended for in their attacking play, especially in the first half, good chances are of little use if they are not then converted.

Sources indicate that although Arteta will recognise that he should have secured three points, Dortmund have taken a well-earned point away from north London. Now, Arsenal need to swiftly refocus on Sunday’s game against Manchester City.

By Ben Knapton | 25 Nov 2026 11:33.

Former Leeds United striker Brian Deane, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has played down the Whites' chances of signing Will Lankshear in the January transfer window.

The former Tottenham Hotspur youngster has taken the Championship by storm since moving to the Riverside Stadium in the summer, scoring 14 goals in 15 second-tier appearances.

Lankshear netted the winner as Middlesbrough beat Swansea City 2-1 on Tuesday night, a result that saw Kim Hellberg's men move one point clear of Wolverhampton Wanderers at the top of the Championship table.

The 21-year-old unsurprisingly sits top of the Championship top scorers charts, three clear of closest challenger Andri Gudjohnsen of Blackburn Rovers in the race for the Golden Boot.

Lankshear's form has inevitably led to speculation surrounding a swift return to the Premier League, with multiple clubs believed to be interested in securing his services, including Leeds.

Former club Tottenham, Arsenal, Brighton & Hove Albion and Newcastle United have also been credited with an interest, although Middlesbrough's £70m asking price could deter suitors.

Now, former Leeds forward Deane - who scored 44 goals in 199 matches for the Whites - has expressed his view that Lankshear should remain at the Riverside Stadium over the winter.

“This is his breakout season, and he is at a good club," Deane told Sports Mole. "Middlesbrough look on course to challenge for promotion, so hopefully he gets there with them.

“He will be ambitious and attract attention from clubs such as Leeds, Brighton and Newcastle. He would be a good addition to a squad. But for his own development, I think he is in a good place at Middlesbrough.”.

Lankshear made just six senior appearances for Tottenham before being sold in a £9.8m deal over the summer, and the striker's contract with Middlesbrough does not expire until 2031.

A young striker scoring for fun in the Championship will always attract glances from top-tier clubs, but Lankshear may struggle to force his way into Daniel Farke's first XI right now.

First-choice pairing Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor boast a respectable nine Premier League goals between them in 2026-27, and as long as both are fit, they will spearhead Farke's 3-5-2 system.

Calvert-Lewin is now in the final 24 months of his contract at Elland Road, but the England international is understood to be close to signing a new Leeds deal.

Lukas Nmecha also provides a steady backup option, although he is due to become a free agent in 2027 and may seek a move away in January if his game-time situation does not improve.

However, Nmecha's proposed exit would then open the door for summer signing Jean-Matteo Bahoya to earn more opportunities, so a winter move for Lankshear would make little sense for all involved.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After another disastrous result last night, I was left scratching my head wondering what can actually be done to solve the problems facing West Ham.
  • I think 50 points might be enough to survive this league!
  • Earlier this week I wrote about the statistics, and they tell the real story behind West Ham’s struggles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After another disastrous result last night, I was left scratching my head wondering what can actually be done to solve the problems facing West Ham. If results continue along this trajectory, the Hammers could find themselves looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom end of the Championship table rather than fighting for promotion. At this rate, even a play-off spot feels optimistic.

I think 50 points might be enough to survive this league!

Earlier this week I wrote about the statistics, and they tell the real story behind West Ham’s struggles.

Shot after shot, chance after chance, attack after attack, and still the ball refuses to go in. Remarkably, despite their wastefulness, the Hammers remain the division’s top scorers. In the last two matches alone, they have struck the woodwork five times.

Against Portsmouth, West Ham registered 19 shots with six on target and failed to score.

According to recent reports, when you add that to the wider picture, the numbers become even more alarming. Across the last six matches, West Ham have taken 130 shots, with 41 on target, and scored only eight goals.

In a recent development, at the opposite end of the pitch, defensive frailties and questionable goalkeeping continue to cost the team. Herrick was barely tested at Fratton Park, but when he was called into action, he was beaten. The goal will almost certainly be recorded as a goalkeeping error. Portsmouth created virtually nothing, yet their only shot on target produced the winning goal.

You can only work with the players available, but it’s difficult to understand how Areola has suffered multiple injuries this season despite not playing a competitive match. Entering the final year of his contract, albeit with a club option for an additional season, he is reportedly earning around £60,000 per week.

According to recent reports, these are concerns that might be understandable in the Premier League. This is the Championship. These players, including the youngsters, should be capable of performing consistently at this level.

Heads – down, negativity growing…time to stop the rot….

The negativity around the club is beginning to grow.

Nuno had to go, and he did. His departure gave Parker an opportunity to reintegrate certain players and rebuild fitness levels through competitive football. To be fair, time has not always been on the latest manager’s side. However, following the international break, he has now had a chance to work with the squad, implement his ideas and stamp his authority on the team.

It has been revealed that the last two matches have to fall at his door. One point from six is simply not good enough. Extend that across his first four games and the record reads two defeats and two draws.

Sources indicate that the much-talked-about fresh manager bounce? It never arrived.

You can see the frustration written all over the players’ faces. The supporters are becoming restless too, and I include myself in that group. I predicted a narrow 1-0 victory for West Ham at Portsmouth, but deep down I feared a repeat of the Preston performance. Unfortunately, those fears proved worse as at least we got a point on Saturday!

Against Preston, West Ham enjoyed 80% possession and recorded 53 touches inside the opposition penalty area. Preston registered just ten.

At Fratton Park, the Hammers dominated possession with 63% of the ball and managed 29 touches in Portsmouth’s box compared to just eight for the home side.

At this point, I’m running out of explanations. The statistics suggest West Ham should be winning games comfortably, but football is decided by goals, not data. Right now, the Hammers can’t convert their dominance into results, and until that changes, the gap between expectation and reality will continue to grow. I’m lost for words. I really am!

Industry observers note that without Zubimendi, Arteta will need to make further decisions regarding his midfield. Like Saka, Zubimendi is good at maintaining good structure, and this is key to Arsenal’s game. Finding a suitable replacement will not be an easy task.

In a recent development, there is some good news. Saliba has overcome his back issue and is once again in the squad. In addition, Max Dowman has served his 3-game ban.

Saliba’s return is particularly timely with City’s attacking threat heading to the Emirates. Arsenal need stability at centre-back, especially if Raya is unavailable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that arsenal have the chance to put Manchester City’s Premier League title hopes under serious pressure this weekend. And with Pep Guardiola’s side already six points behind, this is an opportunity Mikel Arteta cannot afford to waste.

Paul Merson believes another City defeat could effectively end their title challenge. That might sound dramatic in November, but the gap is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

According to recent reports, arsenal welcome City to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, sitting top with 28 points from 11 matches. Their visitors have collected 22 points and gone four consecutive league games without a win.

The Gunners have been diligently building on this lead and can now add to the misery of one of their main competitors.

But Arsenal must be wary of thinking that Manchester City will continue to find life difficult. In fact, Guardiola’s men often thrive in such situations.

Whilst Merson has not ruled out City’s attacking prowess, two players in Rayan Cherki and Jérémy Doku have the ability to turn games around.

However, it is in City’s defensive phase, where more alarm bells should be ringing. The back-line has appeared susceptible and has consequently been exploitable.

And that is where Arsenal must show steel.

Sources indicate that arteta’s team have only scored seven goals in 11 Premier League games, compared to City’s 14. Much can be stated from this stat alone.

Whilst Arsenal have based their title aspirations on great defensive organisation, City have failed to merge their potent attack with the structure that Guardiola requires.

Recent findings suggest that rather than passively allowing City to attack, the Gunners should exploit the instability in their opposition’s defence. Arsenal are more than capable of capitalising on these openings.

Psychologically, City are well aware that they cannot afford to continue to trail. In addition, if Arsenal dominate the early stages of the game, then City may well become even more desperate.

It has been revealed that however, we must not underestimate Guardiola. City have previously turned around games that had gone against them. Arsenal need to ensure this does not happen here.

Merson’s comment that City stands virtually no chance of success following further failure is also quite an assertion.

Arsenal do already appear to have found their feet and can continue to accrue points thanks to their solid defence.

Whilst it would be unwise to totally dismiss City, Guardiola’s side does have sufficient quality to enable them to embark on a successful winning streak. And this cannot be switched off by one result.

As well as having issues to address, Arsenal have also shown problems scoring recently – both in draws with Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund. Against Dortmund, despite having good build-up play, the Gunners were especially frustrated as they failed to score from good opportunities.

And this cannot happen again when they face City.

Whilst this game may not decide the title race, there are still many games left to play, and Arsenal will also go through their own tough periods.

Industry observers note that however, the significance of Sunday’s game should not be downplayed. A win would put nine points between the Gunners and City and further entrench Arsenal’s lead at the top.

It will also compel Guardiola’s men to come from behind.

Despite Merson perhaps being willing to dismiss City, Arsenal must ignore such punditry. They must then go on and produce a good game, seize their opportunities and capitalise on their lead.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.
  • This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • Recent findings suggest that the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

Recent findings suggest that the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

In a recent development, the best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

In a recent development, avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

Recent findings suggest that it did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

It has been revealed that greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

In a recent development, england thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

Recent findings suggest that ioanna Papatheodorou nearly gave Greece the lead when she dribbled past Esme Morgan and Leah Williamson with ease but her powerful strike hit the crossbar. It was a let-off for England, but they made it count by taking the lead just before half-time.

A fine team move ended with an excellent Stanway finish. It was her fifth goal in this qualifying campaign and she is England’s top scorer for 2025-26.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman stated. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

Industry observers note that “That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Sources indicate that the Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

According to recent reports, all eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

Toone promptly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

Sources indicate that that opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven significant-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

With only two points from his first four games, West Ham manager Scott Parker is already coming under pressure, with some even questioning whether he is the right man to take the club forward following last night’s defeat at Portsmouth.

For me, it’s a little premature to be discussing the newly introduced manager’s job security. But make no mistake about it, West Ham are a club in crisis, and there is a lot more wrong than just the manager.

Industry observers note that however, the one thing Parker can control is how he utilises the players at his disposal. And from my seat in Row B at Fratton Park, it was evident that Parker appears no closer to knowing what his best starting XI is.

Concerns in both full-back positions, a lack of creativity through the middle, genuine issues on the left wing and three strikers who can’t score goals.

Sources indicate that west Ham huffed and puffed against Pompey, and no doubt the statistics will have been boosted by a late flurry towards the end of the game when we battered the Portsmouth goal for five minutes. But that could not disguise the fact that we were watching a very, very poor West Ham team.

I had a close-up view of West Ham hams problems from row B at Fratton Park.

Possibly the most disturbing aspect is that neither Preston North End nor Portsmouth, in our last two games, have looked like particularly good teams. The fact of the matter is that you don’t have to be a decent side to beat West Ham.

We now find ourselves closer to the relegation places than automatic promotion, and I’ve seen little to suggest that anyone knows how to turn us around and get us pointing in the right direction.

There’s a substantial game coming up at the London Stadium against Stoke City, but make no mistake about it, the Potters will be licking their lips at the prospect of turning over West Ham.

The Hammers are now starting to look less like promotion certainties and more like Leicester City.

News on Wednesday of a upcoming £375million cash injection targeted to help fund new Newcastle United stadium.

This comes with NUFC fans still waiting to hear definitive official confirmation of what is going to happen regarding stadium intends.

Earlier today The Athletic revealed that the Saudi Arabia PIF are willing to sell 25 per cent of the club, from their 84 percent majority ownership of Newcastle United.

Now The Mail report that their inside sources have told them that ‘This is not a case of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund looking to sell the club, but rather by creating fresh shares…’.

They say that the club’s owners are now getting close to confirming their plans for a fresh Newcastle United stadium AND that today’s exclusive from The Athletic ties in with that.

The Mail stating that the sale of up to a quarter of the total shares in NUFC by Saudi Arabia PIF ‘Would be to inject latest equity to help fund infrastructural developments, including a stadium. With Newcastle said to be valued at £1.5billion, this could equate to a £375million cash injection. PIF would retain their majority ownership…As one source said: ‘This is not about taking cash off the table, it is about funding growth.’.

JP Morgan have now been appointed as advisers in selling part of the Saudi Arabia PIF stake in the club, with The Mail saying that fellow Wall Street firm are also involved, with their role ‘…set to be to provide a loan or other investment to help finance the stadium. As we reported last week, the cost of a fresh home would not be exclusively funded by PIF and co-owner Jamie Reuben, with loans, share challenges and investments all part of the package. The expectation is that a new stadium, rather than a St James’ renovation, will soon be recommended to the club’s owners by the executive team. It will then be up to PIF to sign off on the plans and for a public announcement to be prepared.’.

Aston Villa news: Why Unai Emery's immunity from criticism should no longer exist

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1070 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 12:36.
  • Such is Unai Emery's status at Aston Villa that few would be surprised if the redeveloped North Stand, when completed in 2027, is named after the Spaniard.
  • Taking Villa from relegation candidates in 2022-23 to two Champions League qualifications and a Europa League trophy by the conclusion of 2025-26 arguably deserves that level of recognition.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 12:36.

Such is Unai Emery's status at Aston Villa that few would be surprised if the redeveloped North Stand, when completed in 2027, is named after the Spaniard.

Taking Villa from relegation candidates in 2022-23 to two Champions League qualifications and a Europa League trophy by the conclusion of 2025-26 arguably deserves that level of recognition.

However, despite the expectation that a contract extension past 2029 will be penned in the near future, it will not necessarily strengthen Emery's, or the club's, position in the long term.

Recent findings suggest that tuesday's 1-0 defeat at Galatasaray extended Villa's recent winless streak across all competitions to six matches. They have failed to score in four of those games, and given up leads on three occasions.

According to recent reports, emery is no stranger to an extended blip in form. At the start of both 2025-26 and 2026-27, Villa were off the pace. It is to Emery's credit that Villa became brief Premier League title contenders in a matter of months and still finished in fourth position in last season's standings.

Nevertheless, Villa are now enduring their second extended winless period of the season, raising the question of whether the West Midlands outfit are experiencing a blip or a gradual decline under their most successful manager for nearly 45 years?

With 116 wins from 215 matches, silverware, and delivering moments and experiences that will last a lifetime, Emery is etched into the Villa history books as a God.

Industry observers note that at the same time, this is now a manager of a team that has only recorded 11 wins from his last 27 games in all competitions, as well as losing on 10 occasions. Just seven wins have come from 19 fixtures in 2026-27.

When Villa defeated Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United and Manchester City in relatively quick succession with performances that mixed grit, shrewdness and attacking vigour, the conclusion was that Emery's fresh-looked team had flicked a switch.

However, Villa have regressed as swiftly as they had seemingly improved. When you take into account that Villa had one win in seven between February 1 and March 4, and lost three in a row between April 25 and May 3, this is now the fourth "blip" in less than nine months.

In a recent development, some of the aforementioned statistics will be comparable with managers at similarly-sized clubs in the Premier League and Europe, yet that usually leads to scrutiny over the job that has been conducted over a specific period. Not talk of a contract until 2030 and beyond being signed.

By modern-day standards, Emery is in the unique position of having high control over which players are signed and sold. He essentially has the keys to the footballing side of the club and Villa's fate on the pitch is solely in his hands.

Yet, a 12-time trophy-winning manager of a team that has only earned fewer Premier League points than Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool across a four-year period is frequently telling the media, or anyone who will listen, that Villa should not be competing in the top six, nor for the top-eight positions in the league phase of the Champions League.

Is this an example of Emery trying to reinforce the perception that Villa are underdogs to the so-called Premier League 'big six' because of what is, admittedly, a scandalous PSR scenario, or is it a pre-orchestrated approach to defend his position whenever results do not go Villa's way?

Staying on the subject of things being pre-orchestrated, not enough scrutiny is coming over Villa's and Emery's use of Liverpool's Harvey Elliott and Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho.

It has been revealed that since the summer of 2025, Villa have included £35m and, allegedly, £43m fees with those clubs to sign the players in question should they achieve a specific appearance threshold. Between them, they have made three starts and 13 substitute outings when spending the majority of the time available for selection.

On Tuesday night, Emery omitted Garnacho - who has accumulated fewer than 100 minutes across seven substitute appearances - from the squad for the Galatasaray match, despite naming one fewer substitute than was permitted. Afterwards, he delivered a frank response over the Argentine's chances of earning future game time.

According to recent reports, if Villa do not want to pay vast amounts of money for players, they do not have to. However, are Villa not harming their chances of signing players through similar deals in the future? Why should clubs trust such deals to go through if Emery is choosing not to select such players or is being told not to?

Everything points to Garnacho becoming Elliott 2:0 and the situation deserves some clarity. If an honest assessment cannot be delivered to fans and the media, Emery leaves himself open to persistent questioning and criticism, and it will be warranted.

Of course, the evolving Garnacho saga can change for the better. Excluding Villa's game against Chelsea in December, the winger has seven more chances to feature in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that there can be a rapid upturn in fortunes, too. Villa face Ipswich Town, Everton and Crystal Palace in the Premier League before they welcome Paris Saint-Germain to Villa Park in the Champions League.

However, when Emery is storming down tunnels before the full-time whistle, throwing tantrums in the media and getting increasingly frustrated on the touchline as his team look slow, devoid of ideas and can make 700 passes in a game and not score against a team such as Sunderland, it can be argued that Villa need a change of direction rather than remaining on their current path.

Recent findings suggest that villa have a deep squad with talent that can earn them success in the future, yet they have too many under-performers or players who may simply be tired even at this stage of the season. Whether that is down to Emery, or too much emphasis being placed on players needing to adapt to the "Emery way" before they earn regular starts, it is open to debate.

Regardless, Villa are presently on a downward trajectory under his leadership, and Emery has questions to answer if he is to remain untouchable at a club that want to hand him a contract extension when they could enter December with just three Premier League wins in 2026-27.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has now been revealed what each of the 20 Premier League clubs received from the 2025-26 TV cash payouts.

The information made public via the publication of the EPL’s official 2025-26 annual report.

This report including a breakdown of how much money each of last season’s 20 Premier League clubs banked.

In total, the 20 Premier League clubs received £3,142m for the 2025-26 season.

This is a 10.9% increase on the 2024-25 season.

Banking the most were Arsenal with £198.1m, whilst Wolves received the least with £117.2m.

It has been revealed that the Premier League is actually one of the very fairest major European leagues in terms of the gap between which clubs get the very most and very least. Arsenal getting 1.69 x what Wolves received.

This is the breakdown of the total distributions of £3,142m between the 20 Premier League clubs (in order of placings in the Premier League table for the 2025-26 season):.

£198.1m Arsenal £192.7m Man City £191.3m Man U £182.1m Aston Villa £181.6m Liverpool £170.2m Bournemouth £167.7m Sunderland £161.7m Brighton £160.8m Brentford £163.4m Chelsea £154.5m Fulham £153.7m Newcastle United £147.1m Everton £144.2m Leeds £136.4m Palace £135.9 Forest £136.6m Spurs £127.9m West Ham £118.6m Burnley £117.2m Wolves.

As you can see, some clubs got more than one or more of those that finished above them in the table. This is due to how many times the relative clubs were chosen for live UK coverage, this is the ‘Facility Fees’ portion of the cash.

The Newcastle United total of £153.7m is broken down as:.

UNITED KINGDOM (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £31.9m Facility Fees £20.3m Merit £15.4m.

CENTRAL COMMERCIAL Equal Share £11.2m.

OVERSEAS (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £56.5m Merit £18.4m.

In a recent development, newcastle United received £6.5m less than 2024-25 as they fell eight places in the Premier League table. However, it would have been a far bigger drop without the overall 10.9% increase in the entire share out and the fact that NUFC were selected 31 times for UK TV coverage across 2025-26.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 12:37.
  • Venezia head into their matchday 13 encounter with in-form Bologna seeking a third league victory in four matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo.
  • The Europe-chasing visitors sit 11 places above the Veneto-based club in the Serie A table but will be wary of the Winged Lions' recent improvement in front of their supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 12:37.

Venezia head into their matchday 13 encounter with in-form Bologna seeking a third league victory in four matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo.

The Europe-chasing visitors sit 11 places above the Veneto-based club in the Serie A table but will be wary of the Winged Lions' recent improvement in front of their supporters.

On the surface, Venezia's decision to replace Giovanni Stroppa with Davide Nicola has made little difference to their results, with the Lagunari sitting bottom of the league.

However, a closer look suggests that the home supporters can expect a battling performance when Bologna travel to Venice on Friday.

Still the only Serie A side yet to draw this term, the promoted outfit have suffered 10 defeats in 12 matches, including four since Nicola's appointment in October.

Nonetheless, all six of their points have come from their last three matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo, where they have beaten Napoli (1-0) and Udinese (2-1) either side of a 2-0 defeat to Inter Milan.

That loss to the defending champions came courtesy of own goals from Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal in the final 10 minutes, with the bottom-placed side attempting 12 shots to Inter's 16 and creating two clear-cut chances to the Nerazzurri's three.

Although three matches represent a small sample, those recent performances in Venice suggest that the Lagunari are slowly turning the tide at home, giving Bologna reason for caution ahead of Friday's trip.

Raffaele Palladino's Rossoblu know all about upturns in form, having experienced their own resurgence since Domenico Tedesco was dismissed in mid-September following a winless start to the campaign.

A 1-0 defeat to Napoli at the Maradona proved the final straw for the hierarchy in Bologna, with Palladino inheriting a Felsinei side that had collected just one point from an available 12 across four matches.

Sitting 16th at the time and outside the bottom three only on goal difference, the Rossoblu have since collected 17 points from a possible 24 under Palladino to climb to ninth on 18 points, just three behind sixth-placed Juventus.

Only Lazio (22), AC Milan (19) and Roma (18) have earned more points during that period, underlining Bologna's resurgence since Tedesco's departure as they target a sixth victory in nine league matches.

The travelling supporters will therefore back their in-form side to overcome Nicola's men, although the result may be less straightforward than some anticipate given the Lagunari's steady improvement on home turf.

Toma Basic (muscle), Thierry Correia (thigh), Pasquale Mazzocchi (muscle), Andrea Adorante (hernia), Marin Sverko (hip) and Bartol Franjic (shoulder) are all considered unlikely to feature in gameweek 13.

No player has scored more than twice for the division's lowest scorers, with Akor Adams and Antoine Hainaut netting two apiece to account for half of the Winged Lions' eight league goals.

While Bologna have no individual producing spectacular numbers, they boast a broader spread of match-winners, with Federico Bernardeschi, Samuel Mbangula, Riccardo Orsolini and Tommaso Pobega all scoring twice.

Although Juan Miranda, Nicolo Cambiaghi and Jens Odgaard have yet to score, their respective returns of five, three and two assists underline their importance to the Rossoblu.

However, Bologna must manage without Miranda, who is sidelined alongside Jay Enem (Achilles), Oussama El Azzouzi (thigh) and Emil Holm (thigh).

Venezia possible starting lineup:.

Stankovic; Halhal, Moreno, Juan Jesus; Hainaut, Kike Perez, Sohm, Busio, Haps; Lauberbach, Adams.

Bologna possible starting lineup:.

Skorupski; Darmian, Casale, Theate; Zortea, Ferguson, Pobega, Cambiaghi; Bernardeschi, Orsolini; Odgaard.

Venezia's victories over Napoli and Udinese suggest that their lowly position does not tell the whole story, particularly after they made Inter work for their points in Venice.

However, Bologna's 17-point return from eight matches under Palladino reflects a more sustained improvement, and the visitors should have enough attacking variety to edge Friday's encounter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the face of it West Ham have too few options in key areas of the pitch, meaning that despite their ineffectiveness, the same payers have to be utilised again and again.

Joel Piroe, after another anonymous evening, will probably get selected to start at Saturday simply because of the options available: Neither Taty Castellanos who was invisible in his 10 minutes last night nor Pablo Felipe who is not even making Parker’s squad offer a better option as potential goal scorers. So Piroe’s ineffectiveness is set to continue.

The same applies in the case of  right back Joel Veltman: Albeit through Kyle Walker Peters‘ injury, Scott Parker has very little option but to start the Dutchman again, despite his pretty universally condemned performance at Fratton Park.

Veltman- unable to add much to West Ham’s offensive capabilities.

Footballfancast.com  single out Veltman for special mention:.

“The Dutchman, who is averaging 0.5 key passes and 0.1 dribbles per game, was once again ineffective in possession against Portsmouth before being substituted in the 62nd minute.

Veltman has never produced more than three assists in a season in his career and has not assisted more than one league goal in a season since the 2016/17 campaign with Ajax, which highlights that he is an even bigger problem [than Piroe] as he does not have relevant experience to suggest that he will turn things around.

Parker must, now, drop the defender to the bench to explore his options in that area of the pitch, as the Hammers need more on the ball from the player in that position moving forward.”.

Can’t really argue with that but unless Scott Parker is prepared to start Arne Engels as an emergency right back then the Hammers boss is fresh out of options until Walker Peters recovers. Veltman was the free signing designed to give West Ham cover in the event of injury. We’d not perhaps envisaged him being required to play week in, week out. His failure going forward is likely the reason Jarrod Bowen is having to play so wide.

Just an observation but does seem a trend when Walker Peters is absent, that Bowen hugs the touch line more, knowing his full back is not going to overlap or assist him in the way in which Walker Peters can.

Time, then, for anxious glances to the treatment table to see how Walker Peter’s recuperation from his thigh muscle issue is going.
