Alanyaspor will be looking to halt their alarming slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Konyaspor to GAIN Park on Friday evening.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 12 points from 12 matches, while the visitors occupy 15th place with eight points and will be hoping to close the gap after suffering three consecutive league defeats.

Alanyaspor have endured a difficult period in recent weeks, losing five consecutive league matches and leaving themselves increasingly vulnerable to being dragged into the relegation battle.

The Thunders began that sequence with a 3-0 defeat away to Fenerbahce before suffering a 2-1 home loss against Kocaelispor six days later, and their struggles continued when they travelled to face Genclerbirligi, suffering a humiliating 5-0 defeat, which was followed by a 2-0 home loss to Trabzonspor.

Those results led to Joao Pereira leaving by mutual agreement, with Ugur Ucar subsequently appointed, but the upcoming manager was unable to bring about an immediate improvement as Alanyaspor were beaten 2-1 at Kasimpasa in his first game in charge.

They have now lost five Super Lig matches in a row and are without a win in their last six, drawing one, leaving Ucar with plenty to address as his side attempt to rediscover the form that helped them collect points earlier in the campaign.

Their recent performances have also been particularly disappointing defensively, having conceded 12 goals across their last five league matches, making them the worst-performing side in the division over that period.

The 4-1 victory over 12 Bingolspor in the Turkish Cup is the only positive result the Thunders have recorded during that spell, and just their second home win across all competitions, having won only their opening home league game, drawn two and lost two, leaving them without a league victory on home soil in their last four attempts.

However, Alanyaspor have enjoyed the better of recent meetings between the sides, remaining unbeaten in their last six competitive encounters with Konyaspor while winning each of the last five.

Konyaspor, meanwhile, have also struggled to maintain consistency this season and are four points behind the hosts, having collected just two wins, two draws and eight defeats from their opening 12 league matches.

Ilhan Palut's side have also lost their last three league games, suffering a heavy 4-0 home defeat against Galatasaray before losing 1-0 away to Samsunspor and then 4-2 against Besiktas in their latest outing.

Aside from their poor record in this fixture, the Anatolian Eagles have another concern heading into Friday's encounter, having collected just one point from five away matches this season.

In fact, Konyaspor have failed to score in their last four away matches, losing three of those games by a 1-0 scoreline, with a goalless draw against Kasimpasa coming between those defeats.

The Anatolian side have also failed to win on their last three visits to Alanyaspor, losing the previous two by 2-1 scorelines after drawing 2-2 on their earlier trip.

Calciomercato.com have published a report revealing some of the background on Enzo Maresca, who became Manchester City’s latest manager on July 1st after an incredible successful decade under the iconic Pep Guardiola.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Maresca signed a contract until June 2029, but he confirmed in a press conference on the eve of the Champions League match against Napoli that he could have been the manager of an Italian team today instead.

“In March, April, and May, there were contacts with an Italian team, but not with Napoli. I never spoke to the president of Napoli, I never spoke to anyone,” stated the coach, a native of the province of Salerno.

Continuing in that press conference, the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss spoke rather intriguingly about the possibility of returning to work in Italy one day.

Industry observers note that “You never know. I’m delighted to be here, because this is a great club, an organization that has had three coaches in the last 17 years. This shows how differently we work, compared to my country. For Italian football, however, I say there’s no single solution,” he mentioned.

“If we’re where we are, something needs to change. We need to be a little more courageous. Every time we miss a World Cup or a European Championship, people say everything needs to change, and then nothing ever changes.”.

Excluding Napoli – who last spring were already aware of Antonio Conte’s desire to leave – which club or clubs might have contacted Maresca shortly before the end of last season?

Recent findings suggest that maresca was one of the candidates Gerry Cardinale’s Milan considered, the report claims. The Rossoneri owner made it clear early in his search that he was looking for a coach capable of playing a dominant and attacking style of football.

Names like Andoni Iraola (who ended up at Liverpool) were also floated, but in the end Cardinale opted to go with Ruben Amorim, another coach with ties to Manchester given he had been sacked by United a few months prior.

The other avenue leads to Fiorentina, where Fabio Paratici was looking for a coach with different characteristics than Paolo Vanoli. La Viola’s sporting director had his eye on Maresca, but ultimately the courtship of City and being Guardiola’s successor was too appealing.

  • Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.
  • After just eight minutes, his intends were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.

After just eight minutes, his intends were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

According to recent reports, leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off.

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'.

It has been revealed that 'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he mentioned, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

Industry observers note that 'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'.

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'.

And his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul.

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made.

'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

In a recent development, 'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'.

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in big trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 18:40.
  • Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.
  • The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 18:40.

Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.

The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.

Those remarks prompted criticism from global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the German champions of pursuing a "coordinated strategy" to pressure Musiala and his representatives ahead of possible contract discussions.

However, Bayern have now taken a significant step towards addressing the controversy. Following a meeting on Tuesday, November 24, the club and Musiala's agency, 11WINS, published a statement emphasising their shared commitment to the player's recovery and clarifying an key detail about his medical history.

The announcement comes less than a week after Musiala returned to action during Bayern's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne, having missed almost two months through injury.

In a statement published on their official website on Wednesday, Bayern confirmed that discussions with Musiala's management had taken place the previous day.

"A constructive meeting took place between FC Bayern Munich and the management of Jamal Musiala yesterday (Tuesday)," the club announced.

Industry observers note that "For both sides, the player's health comes above everything else. Musiala is being given full support on his road back.".

The statement also addressed speculation surrounding the timing of the midfielder's neurological symptoms, which became public earlier this year.

Bayern and 11WINS confirmed that Musiala underwent his first examination for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they initially appeared.

Crucially, that examination took place more than two months after the Germany international signed his contract extension until June 2030 on February 14, 2025.

The clarification establishes that the medical concerns arose after the agreement was completed, addressing speculation about whether the condition had been known when the lucrative deal was negotiated.

Bayern added that the examination had been conducted in consultation with the club and its medical department.

The statement concluded by confirming that the two parties had agreed to maintain contact and continue discussions "in a spirit of partnership and trust".

According to Sky Germany, Musiala's representatives Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschaffl attended Tuesday's meeting with Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen, president Herbert Hainer and sporting director Max Eberl.

Notably, honorary president Uli Hoeness and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, whose earlier comments contributed to the controversy, were not present.

The joint statement represents a change in tone following several weeks of increasingly public discussion about Musiala's situation.

Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge had all raised questions about the potential consequences if the attacking midfielder failed to recover his previous form.

Rummenigge was particularly outspoken after Friday's draw with Cologne, suggesting that Bayern might eventually have to reconsider the financial terms of Musiala's contract if his performances did not justify the sums involved.

Those comments attracted criticism from FIFPRO, which argued that the club's senior figures were placing unnecessary pressure on a player dealing with significant health concerns.

The union called for contractual matters to be handled privately and emphasised the importance of respecting agreements already signed by both parties.

Further questions emerged following a report by Suddeutsche Zeitung about a meeting between Hoeness and Musiala's agent during the summer.

According to the German newspaper, Hoeness believed there had been a verbal understanding that the midfielder's contract could be revisited if his condition prevented him from returning to his former level.

Musiala's representatives reportedly interpreted that discussion differently, understanding only that the parties could hold further talks if the player's situation failed to improve.

Tuesday's meeting did not produce any revealed agreement to alter the contract.

Indeed, Eberl told Sky Germany that salary matters had not been discussed, with the immediate focus instead placed on supporting Musiala's return.

The sporting director also expressed confidence that the midfielder could regain his best form, stressing the need to give him time without additional pressure.

Musiala's contract remains valid until 2030, and neither Bayern nor his representatives have declared any changes to its terms.

The joint statement therefore provides an important clarification about the circumstances surrounding the original agreement, while leaving the longer-term contractual questions unresolved.

Liverpool lost their 100% record in this season’s Champions League with defeat at Fenerbahce three weeks ago, and they’ll be aiming to bounce back tonight with victory away to Club Brugge.

For Reds fans of a certain vintage, the Belgian outfit will evoke happy memories of the triumphant 1976 UEFA Cup final and 1978 European Cup final, with this being the first meeting since the latter success at Wembley.

Andoni Iraola’s satisfaction at Sunday’s 4-0 drubbing of Manchester United has been tempered by ongoing injuries to Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch, with no return date set for the midfielder  as he continues to struggle with a heel problem.

The Liverpool head coach spoke of how he ‘enjoyed analysing’ Club Brugge, who go into this game level on points and goal difference with the Reds and have a red-hot striker in Nicolo Tresoldi, who’s already netted 16 times this season (including a hat-trick against Inter Milan).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Iraola has made three changes from the starting XI which thumped Man United on Sunday.

Alisson Becker continues between the sticks, and there’s one change to the defence. It’s a surprising one, too, with Virgil van Dijk omitted from the line-up to allow for the reintroduction of Jeremie Frimpong at right-back.

Ronald Araujo duly shuffles across to centre-back to partner Jeremy Jacquet, with Milos Kerkez on the left.

One alteration in midfield sees Trey Nyoni come in for Alexis Mac Allister, with the teenager lining up next to Dominik Szoboszlai.

The third and final change to the starting XI sees Victor Munoz replace Rio Ngumoha in attack, with Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak all keeping their places.

The trio who are cut from the line-up are all on the substitutes’ bench, which also includes a mixture of youth (Jayden Danns, James McConnell, Lewis Koumas, Luke Chambers) and experience (Joe Gomez, Kostas Tsimikas, Freddie Woodman).

Who did figure 3? Why scientists should make experimental contributions visible

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Highlighting who was responsible for each experiment could be a boost to many researchers’ careers.Credit: miniseries/Getty.
  • I ask this question surprisingly often when reading the literature.
  • Industry observers note that after years of working in experimental cell biology, collaborating with other laboratories, reviewing papers and handling manuscripts as an editor, I have come to recognize that this is more than an inconvenience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Highlighting who was responsible for each experiment could be a boost to many researchers’ careers.Credit: miniseries/Getty.

I ask this question surprisingly often when reading the literature. I might be interested in a particular imaging approach, trying to understand an experiment in detail when reviewing a manuscript or simply want to contact a study author who has experience with a technique. I look at the author list, then the contribution statement, and reach the same conclusion: I have no idea who did the work.

Industry observers note that after years of working in experimental cell biology, collaborating with other laboratories, reviewing papers and handling manuscripts as an editor, I have come to recognize that this is more than an inconvenience. By obscuring who does what in a research project, we are losing an key piece of information about how science is done — and the people who do it.

Digital badges aim to clear up politics of authorship.

Digital badges aim to clear up politics of authorship.

This has become particularly obvious to me as my research has become more collaborative. My projects can involve advanced microscopy, molecular biology, animal experiments and computational analysis, each performed by a different group. This is one of the things I enjoy most about modern science: collaborations allow us to answer questions that none of us could address alone. But they also make individual expertise increasingly difficult to see.

Recent findings suggest that when I started in research 20 years ago, papers generally had fewer authors and the experimental work was performed in one or two laboratories. Today, papers routinely have 10, 20 or more authors, with projects spread across several institutes. A 2024 study1 in Scientometrics found that the mean number of authors on papers in the PubMed database grew by more than 50% between 2000 and 2020 (from 3.99 to 6.25). Author-contribution statements help to delineate individual roles in a project, but only to a point. If five people are listed under investigation, three under methodology and four under analysis, I still cannot tell who performed any one experiment.

Anyone who has spent time at the bench knows that experiments require more than simply following the methods section of a paper.

Recent findings suggest that I have seen young researchers spend months, sometimes years, developing expertise in a technique. When the resulting study is published through a large collaboration, that researcher might become one name among many, credited with investigation or methodology. But those words do not tell the person reading the paper that this is the scientist who knows how this experiment works.

In a recent development, for early-career researchers, that’s a missed opportunity. Publications are not only records of scientific findings, they also demonstrate technical proficiency. Being able to say, “I am an author on this paper”, is valuable. Being identifiable as the person who generated a particular piece of evidence provides a different and, in some circumstances, more useful form of recognition.

Recent findings suggest that and there’s another benefit. As a reviewer and editor, I sometimes have technical questions. The corresponding author is, appropriately, my point of contact. But they might not be the person who performed or directly supervised the experiment I care about and, over time, they might not remember who did. PhD students graduate, postdocs change institutions and collaborations evolve. Five years after publication, identifying the person who remembers exactly how an experiment was performed can be difficult.

In a recent development, we rightly devote enormous attention to reproducibility. We record catalogue numbers for antibodies, identify instruments and software versions and deposit raw data sets. Yet we often fail to record something much simpler: who generated the data. I am not suggesting this as a way of assigning blame when something goes wrong — authorship implies collective responsibility for a published study. I see it instead as a strategy to provide traceability of expertise.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03542-w.

Presently playing for Diambars FC in his homeland, the 16-year-old’s performances have attracted interest from numerous European clubs, but it’s the Reds who’ve won the race for his services, having successfully negotiated an option to sign him in January 2028.

The teenager’s potential was spotted by LFC’s global talent team, who moved quickly to snap him up.

Ndiaye was one of the standout performers for Senegal in their 9-0 trouncing of Cuba at the Under-17 World Cup earlier this week, scoring one goal and supplying two assists as his nation ran riot.

Recent findings suggest that given his nationality and the position that he plays, comparisons with Sadio Mane will be inevitable. If he can go on to have even half the impact that his compatriot enjoyed at Liverpool between 2016 and 2022 (120 goals in 269 appearances), he’ll be adored by the Kop.

Securing his signature will come as a huge fillip for the Reds’ recruitment staff, who’ve snapped up some outstanding young gems in recent years and hopefully have landed another one in Ndiaye.

It’ll obviously be a few years yet before the Senegalese prodigy makes his mark at Anfield, but the early signs are that this represents another terrific coup by LFC.

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose has confirmed Junior Kroupi has been reinstated to the Europa League squad ahead of Thursday’s clash against Celta Vigo.

The France international was initially named in the Europa League squad despite undergoing foot surgery in the summer.

However, Kroupi’s absence allowed Bournemouth to use UEFA’s temporary injury replacement rule to include Ben Gannon-Doak for the first four games in the league phase.

Kroupi returned to action last month, but as a result of Gannon-Doak’s inclusion in the Europa League squad, he was unable to feature in the 3-1 win over Sparta Prague at the start of the month.

Rose has now confirmed Kroupi has been brought back into the Europa League squad, meaning Gannon-Doak will drop out for the final four league phase matches unless there are any further injury replacement opportunities.

Alex Scott is also available to make his first Europa League appearance since matchday one after returning from a thigh injury with a substitute appearance in Saturday’s 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

"Everyone is ready,” Rose mentioned. "We have no new injuries ahead of tomorrow's game.

“We are glad to have Alex and Junior back and available.".

Industry observers note that when asked whether the pair will start in Vigo, Rose said: "It could be possible, but also maybe not. We will see".

In regard to absentees, the Cherries are without the injured trio of Julian Araujo, Juanlu Sanchez and Alex Toth.

Bournemouth are currently enjoying the longest winning run in the club's history after recording a ninth consecutive victory in all competitions at the weekend.

They also boast a perfect record in their maiden European campaign, having won their four league phase matches by a combined 11-2 scoreline.

As a result, they head into matchday five in second spot in the Europa League league phase and five points clear of the teams sitting just outside the top eight.

The Blues have kept just three clean sheets across 14 games in all competitions so far this season, and must make changes in January to turn their recent form around.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that newly introduced centre-backs have to be the priority for Alonso if he wants to keep his job as Chelsea manager.

Concerns have already grown about the performances of Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana, while a serious lack of depth in the position has left Chelsea with little option to change.

As a result, big prepares are being put in place for the January transfer window, with at least one newly introduced centre-back expected to be brought in to support Alonso's plans.

The lack of physicality in the absence of Maxence Lacroix has seen Chelsea's defence bullied by big, physical strikers in Brian Brobbey and Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

As a result, the addition of more capable centre-backs has risen to the top of Chelsea's list of priorities, and work is ongoing in the background to strengthen their side.

"Chelsea are so weak defensively and that is now becoming clear every single week," Brown told Football Insider.

"They conceded four goals at home against a Leeds side who have struggled to score much at all this season, and that has got to be a concern for everybody involved.

"Defensively, they are all over the place, and it's becoming clear that the options they've got at the back are not good enough for where they want to be.

"Nobody ever wins anything if they cannot defend, it might not be pretty or fashionable, but it's the most vital part of any successful team.

"There's no way Chelsea are going to be able to compete for any major silverware if they have such clear concerns at the back.

"So, I'm sure they will already be working to identify players who can come in and improve them at centre-back, because it has got to be a priority for them in January.

"If they don't address their weaknesses, results aren't going to get any better, and then Xabi Alonso will be under serious pressure.".

Chelsea's recent results have piled pressure on Alonso's position in the dugout, with large sections of the fans already asked questions about the manager's role.

Complications surrounding the Blues' tactical setup and player selection have led to growing concerns, while recent results have done little to ease the calls for his head.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City's main sponsors Etihad only have a "remote chance" of success if they decide to take legal action against the Premier League.

That is according to former Everton chief executive and ex-Premier League board member Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the league have no reason for concern over the issue.

Etihad and Etisalat, two of City's biggest sponsors, have threatened to sue the Premier League over their guilty verdict on the club's financial charges.

However, Wyness feels that it is likely just a "tactic" from the pair to try and heap the pressure on the Premier League to problem a more lenient punishment to City.

Premier League clubs have voted to cover the cost of legal defence for the Premier League's five directors, should Etihad end up taking them to court.

City and Nottingham Forest were the only two clubs to vote against that notion, with the other 18 all in favour of trying to protect the league's directors.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy advising elite clubs – believes that Etihad's threat is an attempt to make it as difficult as possible for the Premier League to punish City.

The threat of legal action would potentially "increase the cost" of the league issuing a sanction, as they could potentially then face a compensation payment to the club's sponsors.

However, speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained how Etihad's chances of success are hugely limited.

"I think there's a remote chance of success. I don't think it's a great chance at all, but this is all about increasing the cost and making the battle personal," he stated.

"That's what we're seeing right now. And as costs go up across the whole legal complications, in fact, I'm speaking on a panel next Thursday about the growing cost of legal defence right now.

"That's just a genuine tactic that we're seeing from Etihad, and the ownership group at City, to try and make the pain even harder.

It has been revealed that "That's what this is all about. So I don't think there's going to be a great chance of success, but nevertheless, it's going to be very, very expensive to defend.".

Football Insider revealed last week that Man City are "confident" of sealing an agreement over a newly introduced contract for Matheus Nunes sooner rather than later.

Sources say that there is a "willingness" from all parties to get the deal done, with talks already underway for Nunes to stay at the Etihad Stadium beyond 2028.

The Portuguese remains happy in Manchester, and the club continue to value him and his versatility within the squad.

Nunes has become adept in the right-back role in recent years, and is a valuable part of City's project under Enzo Maresca.

#129735. Man United are in the relegation zone on merit and will need all of Mauricio Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it - they are chronically short of form and have forgotten how to win, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Man United are in the relegation zone on merit and will need all of Mauricio Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it - they are chronically short of form and have forgotten how to win, writes CHRIS WHEELER

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.
  • What can he do to improve this shambles of a team?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.

What can he do to improve this shambles of a team? What could anyone do? United could change their head coach every game, but without the tools to do the job, the result will be largely the same.

According to recent reports, chief executive Omar Berrada said in an interview during the week that United have improved since the summer, but who is he trying to kid? They are in the relegation zone on merit, and it will need all of Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it.

He emerged from the tunnel shortly before 4.30pm here dressed smartly in blue, and after greeting Andoni Iraola and his staff, spent a few moments gathering his thoughts while You'll Never Walk Alone echoed around Anfield.

It has been revealed that the game initiative was in tatters inside 13 minutes, though, as he watched United go two goals and one man down. There was much finger wagging from Pochettino when Leny Yoro was somewhat harshly sent off, but the decision was never going to be overturned and nor should it be used to mask another United debacle.

As the enormity of the task he has taken on dawned upon him in the second half, the Liverpool fans taunted: 'Poch is the wheel.'.

Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Man United head coach ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

The manner of the display was a microcosm of why United are mired in the relegation zone.

Pochettino made two changes to the line-up from Michael Carrick's last game in charge against Aston Villa, and the biggest of them backfired spectacularly.

Giving Matthijs de Ligt his Premier League start for more than a year against Liverpool at Anfield felt like a gamble as he replaced Harry Maguire in central defence.

'When I saw Matthijs de Ligt's name on the team-sheet I was absolutely stunned,' admitted former United defender Gary Neville on Sky Sports, citing De Ligt's performance on his only start since last November in the Champions League defeat by Como in October.

However, the Dutchman was at fault for misreading the situation that led to Yoro being sent off in the eighth minute for the foul on Alexander Isak that saw Dominik Szoboszlai fire Liverpool ahead from a free-kick, and was the nearest United defender to Florian Wirtz when he hooked in the second shortly afterwards.

De Ligt got away with falling flat on his face and allowing Isak a free run on goal just after the hour mark, but couldn't stop Bradley Barcola's cross going through his legs when Rio Ngumoha scored the third shortly afterwards.

The nightmare was complete when his ill-judged pass to Joshua Zirkzee let in Liverpool for Victor Munoz to make it 4-0.

Pochettino's other change was to leave out Amad Diallo - who has claimed a couple of memorable goals against Liverpool but hasn't scored for United in nearly a year - and play Patrick Dorgu on the left.

Dorgu returned from injury to head a dramatic late equaliser in Carrick's final game in charge, but he was deemed to be unfit for duty by Denmark who sent him home during the international break.

He started on the left side of attack but switched to left-back when Yoro was sent off and Pochettino reshuffled what is statistically the worst defence in Europe as he tried to avoid a bloodbath.

Matthijs de Ligt (right) endured a nightmare game at centre-back as United were thumped.

Pochettino's response to a horror start was to send on Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo, his best attacker, to provide extra protection for De Ligt.

Recent findings suggest that having started the game in United's familiar 4-2-3-1 formation, he switched to 5-3-1. Moving to a back-five when your team only has 10 men felt like damage limitation.

It needed some excellent saves from Senne Lammens - not to mention a crucial block by Maguire to send Isak's effort over the bar before half-time - to spare United from an embarrassing defeat on a par with the seven and five goal humiliations at the hands of Liverpool in recent years.

Even so, after seeing his team record a pitiful xG of 0.14 in a first half that saw United have one shot on target and four touches in the Liverpool box, he knew they had to pose more of an attacking threat if only to relieve the pressure on their defence.

Zirkzee replaced the anonymous Matheus Cunha at half-time in the hope that he could hold the ball up better, but the xG rose only marginally to 0.63 by the end compared to Liverpool's 4.38.

Pochettino sent on Mason Mount and Noussair Mazraoui for Youri Tielemans and Dorgu in the 65th minute, and they had only been on the pitch for a matter of seconds when Ngumoha got Liverpool's third.

Senne Lammens produced multiple save to prevent the scoreline from further embarrasment.

There are so many problems piled up for Pochettino, it will be difficult to know where to start when he returns to his desk at Carrington on Monday ahead of this week's Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal.

Recent findings suggest that this is a team chronically short of form and confidence that has forgotten how to win. There are only so many changes he can make with the squad available until the January transfer window, so the Argentine is stuck with what he's got until then.

But United have simply got to stop giving up early goals. It was a problem that plagued Carrick against Atletico Madrid, Como, Roma and Villa, and any hope that Pochettino could stop the rot disappeared inside eight minutes here.

Yoro's red card was also United's fourth in the last eight games (and his second), which is another bad habit they will have to kick if Pochettino is going to turn this season from hell around.

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has offered a revealing assessment of his defensive hierarchy after substituting Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger at half-time during Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Los Blancos were trailing 1-0 at the Santiago Bernabeu when Mourinho made three changes at the interval, withdrawing both experienced centre-backs alongside Aurelien Tchouameni. Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen entered in defence, while Jude Bellingham replaced the French midfielder.

The decision preceded a remarkable turnaround. Madrid scored five unanswered goals in the second half, with Bellingham, Federico Valverde, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior contributing to a victory that maintained their perfect Champions League record after five matches.

Although Mourinho insisted that the improvement was primarily down to a collective change in mentality, his explanation for replacing Militao and Rudiger offered an insight into why Konate and Huijsen have established themselves as his preferred central-defensive partnership.

The Portuguese coach acknowledged that the two younger defenders currently benefit from greater match sharpness, while identifying specific qualities that make them particularly valuable to his system.

Speaking to Movistar after the match, Mourinho explained that his decision had been influenced by several factors, including the yellow cards shown to Rudiger and Tchouameni during the opening period.

"A bit of everything," he mentioned when asked whether the substitutions were motivated by fitness, disciplinary concerns or a desire to change the game.

"We had two players on yellow cards in a game against some very quick players, which was a risk.".

However, Mourinho's subsequent assessment was arguably more significant for the two defenders who had been withdrawn.

"Obviously, the two centre-backs who have been playing more regularly are in a better rhythm," he continued.

It has been revealed that "Dean is our best player at bringing the ball out from the back, Konate is playing pretty well... and I thought those changes could help us.".

Those comments underline the advantages currently enjoyed by Huijsen and Konate, who have become Mourinho's regular pairing since the beginning of the campaign.

Huijsen's ability to progress possession from defence is particularly vital in a Madrid side expected to dominate the ball, while Konate provides the physical presence and defensive intensity required when the team presses high.

Both qualities were evident in the second half against PSV, when Madrid pushed their defensive line forward and prevented the Dutch visitors from progressing comfortably through midfield.

Mourinho nevertheless resisted the suggestion that his defensive substitutions alone had transformed the contest.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager also credited Bellingham's introduction and a collective improvement in pressing, explaining that his players had struggled to win individual battles before the interval.

It has been revealed that "The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho noted. "We made changes, yes, and Jude is a different kind of player who gives us what we lacked in the first half, but collectively we were better in the second half.".

Sources indicate that his explanation makes it difficult to interpret the removal of Militao and Rudiger as an outright rejection of either player. Yet publicly highlighting the superior rhythm and individual qualities of their competitors offers a clear indication of the current pecking order.

The situation is particularly delicate for Rudiger, whose contract expires in June 2027.

The 33-year-old German has found regular opportunities difficult to secure under Mourinho, and reports in Spain have suggested that Real Madrid are increasingly unlikely to offer him another extension.

His experience remains an asset, particularly across a demanding season involving several competitions, but his reduced role raises questions about whether he will remain at the Bernabeu beyond next summer.

Militao faces a different challenge.

The Brazil international remains under contract until June 2028, although his recent career has been disrupted by two serious anterior cruciate ligament injuries and further muscular problems.

He has played only five minutes in La Liga this season, with his Champions League appearances providing most of his opportunities to regain competitive sharpness.

Recent findings suggest that tuesday's meeting with PSV represented another chance to demonstrate his readiness for a more prominent role. Instead, his involvement ended after 45 minutes as Mourinho turned to the partnership that has largely carried Madrid's defence this season.

The Brazilian's limited playing time makes the manager's comments about rhythm particularly relevant. Regaining his previous level requires regular appearances, but those opportunities are difficult to obtain while Konate and Huijsen continue to perform.

Huijsen's emergence has already complicated Militao's attempts to recover a starting place, with the Spain international establishing himself as a central figure in Mourinho's defensive plans.

Konate, meanwhile, has made a strong impression following his arrival from Liverpool, offering the combination of athleticism and defensive aggression that the Portuguese coach values.

Sources indicate that the two established internationals therefore face different uncertainties. Rudiger must consider his future as his contract approaches its conclusion, while Militao has more time remaining on his deal but needs to demonstrate that he can compete consistently for a starting position.

Mourinho has not revealed plans to sell either defender, and Tuesday's substitutions should not be regarded as confirmation of their departures.

However, the manager's unusually explicit assessment of his centre-backs has reinforced the challenge facing both players: Konate and Huijsen currently possess the match rhythm, tactical qualities and established partnership that make them difficult to displace.

Menopause can speed up brain ageing — hormone therapy might protect it

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1080 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hormonal changes during menopause could explain why Alzheimer’s disease affects more women than men.
  • Recent findings suggest that some types of hormone therapy for menopause are linked to better memory performance and a reduced risk of mild cognitive impairment, according to data presented at a neuroscience conference that began on 14 November.
  • The research is part of a series of studies presented at the Society for Neuroscience’s Neuroscience 2026 conference that reveal differences in cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression on the basis of biological sex or life stage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hormonal changes during menopause could explain why Alzheimer’s disease affects more women than men. Credit: Maskot/Getty.

Recent findings suggest that some types of hormone therapy for menopause are linked to better memory performance and a reduced risk of mild cognitive impairment, according to data presented at a neuroscience conference that began on 14 November. The findings suggest that some therapies could be protective against the brain changes that often precede Alzheimer’s disease, say the authors, although more research is needed to confirm this effect.

The research is part of a series of studies presented at the Society for Neuroscience’s Neuroscience 2026 conference that reveal differences in cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression on the basis of biological sex or life stage. The studies have not been peer reviewed.

In a recent development, women are twice as likely to develop AD than are men. But the reasons for these sex differences are poorly understood and poorly studied, say researchers in the field. “The women’s health gap is huge,” Liisa Galea, a neuroscientist at the University of Toronto in Canada, told reporters at the conference, which was held in Washington DC. Part of the problem is that studies often do not analyse sex differences, she adds.

Researchers think that hormonal changes that happen during menopause could partly explain why the disease affects women and men differently. For instance, going through menopause early, between 40 and 45 years old, is thought to increase a woman’s risk of cognitive decline and developing AD. Some studies have found that oestrogen — which decreases during menopause — has a protective effect on the brain.

Mateja Perović, a neuroscientist at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health in Toronto, and her team wanted to know whether menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), which is used to supplement oestrogen levels and treat symptoms of menopause, can slow cognitive ageing and reduce the risk of developing AD. Perović notes that previous studies have showed mixed results, but these studies had not differentiated between the different types of MHT1.

Industry observers note that the team analysed the cognitive function of around 14,000 women who received different types of MHT or none at all2. They also compared cognitive function between women using MHT who had a genetic risk of developing AD and those who didn’t.

In a recent development, they found that oestradiol-based treatments — which contain a compound that is chemically identical to the oestrogen produced by the body — were associated with better episodic memory in women without cognitive impairment than were treatments containing a mix of natural and synthetic oestrogens. Episodic memory refers to the ability to learn and recall information. A deficit in this can be an early symptom of AD. Women who did not receive any MHT also showed better episodic memory than did those who received the mixed-oestrogen treatments.

Oestradiol-based MHT also showed benefits for women who were not genetically predisposed to AD and had mild cognitive impairment, whereas the mixed-oestrogen MHT did not.

Recent findings suggest that both treatment types were beneficial for other types of long-term memory function compared with no MHT for women who had mild cognitive impairment and carried a gene called APOE4, which is linked to an increased risk of developing AD. But MHT use did not affect the risk of progressing to dementia, suggesting that the treatments might improve a person’s cognitive function without preventing the disease.

According to recent reports, when the researchers looked at structural brain changes using imaging techniques, they found that women with the APOE4 gene who took oestradiol had higher cortical thickness and less white-matter damage than did women not receiving MHT. Decreased cortical thickness, caused by the loss of neurons, is associated with decreased brain function and can be an early indicator of cognitive impairment. The findings suggest that oestradiol-based MHT might be particularly beneficial for women at higher risk of developing AD, notes Perović.

According to recent reports, mia Schaumberg, who studies healthy brain ageing at the University of the Sunshine Coast in Sippy Downs, Australia, notes it is promising that research is considering individual risk factors, such as genetics and differences in MHT composition, when looking at women’s cognitive health. “It is starting to gain the attention that it deserves,” she adds.

However, Susan Davis, an endocrinologist and researcher at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia, says that the effect of MHT on AD risk needs to be investigated in a randomized clinical trial to validate the findings of this study.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” mentioned Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

“I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”.

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Recent findings suggest that sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

According to recent reports, he told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a massive difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”.

The veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”.

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Industry observers note that palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has been tipped to become England's greatest ever player by former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Jamie O'Hara, who believes the 23-year-old is already a better footballer than Harry Kane.

Bellingham produced another outstanding Champions League performance on Tuesday, scoring a spectacular goal and providing an assist in Real Madrid's 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven at the Bernabeu.

The England international improvised a remarkable volley with the outside of his boot after the ball bounced back towards him on the edge of the penalty area, later describing the strike as the best goal of his career.

His performance prompted an enthusiastic reaction from O'Hara, whose admiration for Bellingham is accompanied by a growing frustration that English football supporters have never had the opportunity to watch him regularly in the Premier League.

Speaking on talkSPORT's The Sports Bar, O'Hara made a bold prediction about Bellingham's international career.

"He's going to be England's greatest ever player. Ever. He's better than Harry Kane, a better player than Kane," the former Tottenham midfielder said.

Recent findings suggest that coming from a former Spurs player, the comparison carries weight given Kane's achievements for both club and country. England's all-time leading goalscorer has established himself as one of the finest centre-forwards of his generation, although Bellingham's influence on matches comes from a different position.

The Real Madrid midfielder has registered seven goals and five assists in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, with only Kylian Mbappe directly contributing to more goals for Los Blancos in La Liga.

His ability to influence proceedings from midfield while regularly producing decisive contributions in the final third makes him a valuable player for England. By the time Euro 2028 comes around, Bellingham should be approaching the peak years of his career, with considerable experience of European football already behind him.

O'Hara also described it as a "travesty" that Premier League supporters do not get to watch the midfielder in domestic action every week. However, fellow pundit Jason Cundy suggested that Bellingham's decision to develop his career outside England may have contributed to his success.

It has been revealed that unlike many of England's leading internationals, Bellingham has built his reputation almost entirely outside his homeland. He left Birmingham City for Borussia Dortmund in 2020 at the age of 17 before joining Real Madrid three years later.

His time in Germany allowed him to establish himself as a regular at Champions League level while still a teenager. At Madrid, he won both La Liga and the Champions League in his debut campaign, scoring 23 goals across all competitions.

The prospect of Bellingham eventually playing in the Premier League appears increasingly distant, with Real Madrid reportedly in advanced negotiations over a new long-term contract.

According to The Athletic, the Spanish giants intend to announce an agreement before the end of the calendar year, with Bellingham expected to receive a significant increase on his current annual salary of approximately £12.6m.

His existing deal already runs until June 2029, meaning Real Madrid are under little immediate pressure to negotiate. Their willingness to offer improved terms more than two and a half years before its expiry reflects the importance they attach to retaining the midfielder.

According to recent reports, for England, there is little sporting reason to regret Bellingham's absence from the Premier League. He is developing at one of Europe's most demanding clubs and gaining experience in the latter stages of major competitions. The disappointment expressed by O'Hara is understandable from a spectator's perspective, but the Three Lions may benefit from the unconventional route their midfielder has taken.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United are set to fund the building of a fresh stadium using “debt from the market” rather than PIF’s own funding into the project.

That is according to former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that Goldman Sachs’ involvement in the project is a “very positive sign.”.

This comes after the news that representatives from the American investment bank were present on Tyneside recently for a meeting with the club hierarchy over the new stadium plans.

Wyness outlined that the debt Newcastle are set to take on to fund the project is nothing to worry about for fans, given that will be invested into newly introduced revenue streams.

Recent reports have estimated that the Magpies’ fresh ground is likely to cost around £1.3billion to build, with a planned capacity of around 65,000.

The North East outfit have played at their current St James’ Park home since 1892, but are now in line to move to a fresh site at Leazes Park within the next few years.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy business advising elite clubs – believes that Newcastle’s newly introduced ground will become a “showpiece stadium” for the North East.

The Scottish businessman is pleased to see the club planning to use Goldman Sachs to help fund the project, rather than solely relying on PIF’s own finances.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained how the debt from loans for the stadium would be good debt to take on.

“Well it's interesting with Goldman being present because it does point to the fact that this would be financed with debt from the market rather than PIF actually funding it themselves,” he said.

“So that means that this would not be PIF investment purely into the club which is what we talked about last week. It's actually a very positive sign that this would be debt on the club.

“Because, they could afford it with a fresh stadium and we've always discussed the fact that when you go take on more debt, as long as you're putting it into things that are increasing your revenue streams, that's okay.

According to recent reports, “It's when you start taking on debt to pay costs is the real problem. In this case, I'm sure it is going to be a showpiece stadium. It's been 18 months I've been talking about this now. So we're all keen to see it.”.

Former Manchester City financial advisor Stefan Borson recently told Football Insider that Newcastle could lose around “£75million” each year just from interest rates on their loans for the stadium project.

The football finance expert pointed to the 2.5 per cent interest that Tottenham paid when building their new stadium, and outlined that Newcastle would be lucky to pay less than double that in today’s financial climate.

Borson believes that the loan needed for Newcastle’s stadium plans could creep up to the £1.5bn mark by the time yearly interest is factored into the total.

The Magpies’ hierarchy are maintaining that a newly introduced ground is a necessary step to help the club reach the next level, but it is set to cost an eye-watering sum of money.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rangers are having serious concerns about Connor Barron's lack of playing time since his loan move to Middlesbrough.

The 24-year-old left Ibrox on a season-loan loan deal during the summer after it became clear that he would not play a part in Derek McInnes' plans at Ibrox.

The door was left open to a potential return to Ibrox, while a permanent move to Boro remains on the cards, but his lack of minutes could scupper both of those possibilities.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Rangers hoped Barron would play regularly, either so he could improve their side or command a high fee.

Instead, the midfielder has failed to make a single appearances for Boro, even off the bench, with his only minutes this season coming during Rangers' Conference League qualifyers.

That has been flagged as a serious concern at Ibrox, where they are considering their next steps as they remain keen for Barron to play regular football this season.

Football Insider revealed back in September that Rangers are planning to evaluate Barron's loan spell in January, when he will have had time to settle in the Championship.

As the mid-season transfer window nears, his lack of involvement remains a problem despite Kim Hellberg's positive words, and a return to Ibrox is now firmly on the cards.

Any recall from his loan spell would be unlikely to see Barron thrust into McInnes' plans, but his lack of minutes for Boro could open the door to another loan spell.

"Rangers will have serious concerns if Connor Barron is not playing for Middlesbrough," Brown told Football Insider.

"It was clear he wasn't going to be part of their plans, but they sent him on loan to see if he could impress elsewhere, and then they could take their next steps afterwards.

"Whether that would see him come back and have another go at Rangers, or it would lead to a permanent move for a massive fee, that will have been in the club's thinking.

"But if he's gone away and can't get a game, you have to ask serious questions about his ability and whether he is good enough.

"That's a problem for Rangers, because it raises questions about their recruitment, but it also means it might be difficult for them to deal with his return.

"Maybe it's something that could happen in January and he could move elsewhere so they don't have to tear up their aims, but it's not a situation they wanted to be in.".

After it became clear that Barron was not wanted as part of McInnes' looks for the season, preparations were put in place to move the midfielder on, before he joined Middlesbrough.

Despite eventually agreeing to let him leave on loan, Rangers had been keen to do a permanent deal in a bid to raise funds from the midfielder's sale.

Football Insider revealed during the summer that Rangers would listen to "significant offers" for Barron, with a fee of around £8million likely to be required to lure him away.

Despite attracting no suitors at that lofty price tag, there was later optimism at Ibrox that an impressive loan spell could inspire clubs to spend big on a deal.

Instead, he has struggled at Boro, and Rangers could be forced to reevaluate their position and Barron's asking price if he returns in the near future.

  • Chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson, chief financial officer Simon Capper and chief operating officer Brad Miller were on stage discussing head coach Matthias Jaissle, transfers and the prospect of a newly introduced stadium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 10:59 EST, 24 November 2026.

Newcastle United’s hierarchy addressed supporters at a ‘United We Stand’ event in the shadow of St James’ Park this week.

Chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson, chief financial officer Simon Capper and chief operating officer Brad Miller were on stage discussing head coach Matthias Jaissle, transfers and the prospect of a newly introduced stadium.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was also in the room, and here is his rundown of all the key topics….

‘Arsenal (2-2 draw) felt like a real step forward in the second-half, you felt the energy change in the stadium. But as positive as it was, the biggest feeling we have right now is one of frustration, because the first half wasn't good.

Sources indicate that ‘We have seen that a few times already this season. An outstanding first half against Hull and a difficult second half. Maybe at Tottenham, 90 minutes straight, really good. Crystal Palace, the second-half very good, first half not.

‘So we're definitely trying to find consistency and Saturday was positive. The team felt like they owed that performance to the fans in the second-half. The frustration is that we didn't see that for 90 minutes.’.

Sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson were among the members of the Newcastle hierarchy to answer questions from fans on Monday.

The discussion came in the wake of a promising Saturday performance against Arsenal.

HOPE: It would have been easy for Wilson to say, ‘Wasn’t Saturday great? We build from here’. Instead, he gave an honest assessment of where the team is at - because progress cannot really be achieved by playing well for 45 minutes here and there. It felt like a little warning shot, and a fair one.

Sources indicate that ‘I want to be really clear (about Vision 2030). I think sometimes it has been misreported as, “Oh, I’m guaranteeing we're going to win by 2030”. No, what I have is guaranteed is that we're in the conversation.

‘(Re 2.0) We set up with a plan that was very coherent of what we wanted to accomplish this summer. Not incremental change, but necessary and significant change. We lost three players who were crucial contributors to the past season.

Industry observers note that ‘We set out on a direction under Ross' leadership where we would have a different set of expectations that recognised financial reality. We articulated a vision for the squad here that would be organised around some young talent, who we expect to grow here.

Recent findings suggest that ‘So I’m delighted with the job Ross did. We executed that strategy superbly. Not everything that we set out to do was accomplished. We went hard on Johan Manzambi and didn't succeed. We went hard on Victor Munoz, didn't succeed, despite thinking we were going to land both of those at one point. But also had successes that we had not anticipated.’.

Recent findings suggest that HOPE: Wilson also spoke about the strategy of bringing down the squad’s average age, and there appeared to be no panic or concern over the so-far indifferent impact of summer additions. It has been noted by many that on Saturday, in the second half, no fresh signings were involved apart from goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek. For me, you cannot judge players over three months (look at Lewis Hall) but the major price tags attached to some of the young arrivals has raised expectation. Jaissle and the hierarchy need the likes of Matias Fernandez-Pardo, in particular, to start impacting, if questions over summer business are to quieten.

Sources indicate that ’In simple terms, the club had maxed out its credit card in the first few years under the new ownership. We had complied with PSR but it had been incredibly tight, and that forced us to sell at an undervalued price people like Elliot Anderson. We didn’t want to and we didn't want to be there again.

It has been revealed that ‘So we had to do something differently. The good news is that the Premier League has changed their rules so that there's a bit more headroom now. We’re comfortably within those and we're also comfortably within what we've agreed with UEFA (Newcastle were fined earlier this year). So we're in a really good place. That's the work that David and Ross had talked about in terms of 2.0.

‘That allows us to actually continue to invest and trade. It means that we've got no imperative to sell somebody in January. And it gives us the ability, depending on where we are in the league at the end of this season, to invest again at a proportionate level, depending on what European competition you qualify for.’.

In a recent development, HOPE: The message was clear - there is scope to spend in January and next summer. Newcastle should use that to target goals in the Upcoming Year.

New Magpies coach Mathias Jaissle was also under the microscope in the shadow of St James' Park.

According to recent reports, ‘Eddie Howe was a workaholic and he put his heart and soul into the job. So we needed someone who would work hard and the players would not notice a drop off. Matthias works incredibly hard.

‘Eddie was also outstanding on the grass, an elite coach. Again, our players couldn't feel, “Eddie’s gone and they've got another guy who doesn't coach”. Matthias is an expert, elite coach.

It has been revealed that ‘From a transfer perspective, the head coach at Newcastle always has the final say in any player who comes in. Matthias puts a lot of effort into that - convincing players and making sure they're the right character fit for him. He’s thrown himself into all things Newcastle and we enjoy working with him a lot.’.

‘Matthias is a clear winner. And you know winners, they win over time. I have a high, high conviction we're going to win under his leadership. I don't think I've ever had the conviction more that we're going to win together than I do right now.’.

It has been revealed that HOPE: It is a bold statement from Hopkinson on the back of one win in seven, but the support for Jaissle is clear. He will (and should) be given time, despite an inconsistent start that has included a couple of horror shows. It was also interesting to note Wilson’s reference to Jaissle’s heavy involvement in transfers, on the back of a week in which the head coach let it be known he wanted more control over transfers.

‘This decision is going to last forever. It will outlast our lifetime. It’s that enormity that means we are taking a little bit of time now.

‘Is it going to allow us to compete with the top clubs? Are we going to be able to do it from a financial perspective? Is it going to be transformative for all of our fans, the city and for the region? For all of those reasons, we are very purposely taking our time. But whether we stay at St James’ Park or move, it will be absolutely fantastic.’.

Newcastle continue to mull key decisions on the renovation of their stadium in a bid to unlock upcoming revenue for the club.

According to recent reports, ‘We need it (larger stadium) for the revenue a new stadium will unlock. This is a generational decision and will define the next era of this club. It’s going to be really expensive. We’re advancing significantly into clearly defined options. This is a project with global significance.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We've spent a lot of time with New York bankers recently thinking through how we might do this and what options we can consider. I can assure you we're working on this every day. I hope we will have something concrete to share with you soon.’.

HOPE: There was ‘no update’ but the subtext of the discussion was very definitely geared towards a fresh stadium. I understand this is the direction of travel now, and Hopkinson confirming our story from last week about the high-level talks with Goldman Sachs over how to finance a new stadium demonstrates how advanced the project is.

Overall, the tone of the night was one of ‘we have a strategy, stick with us’. It was very different 12 months ago, when the mood in the room was one of huge optimism and excitement at the unveiling of a new executive team ahead of a Champions League campaign.

Now, it feels like all involved - supporters and those on the inside - realise that this part of the journey will not be easy. That was reflected in the message conveyed.

Arsenal will only accept offers for Viktor Gyokeres if they believe they can find a replacement who will do a better job.

The 28-year-old has struggled for regular game time so far this season, and is no longer regarded as the first-choice striker in Mikel Arteta's side, raising fresh concerns.

So far this season, he has started just seven games across all competitions and scored just three goals, raising questions about his long-term future at the Emirates.

However, former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Gyokeres still has a role to play for Arsenal and will not be forced out unless a replacement emerges.

Arteta is happy with the Sweden international's contributions, and was full of praise following an impressive goalscoring display against Borussia Dortmund midweek.

Gyokeres, meanwhile, is working to regain his place in the Arsenal starting XI and is not planning to push for a move any time soon as he remains a strong option for Arteta.

Football Insider revealed last month that Arsenal's admiration of Nicolo Tresoldi could force them into a decision over Gyokeres' future, as the deal hinges on his potential exit.

However, they may opt against signing Tresoldi as they are content with the Sweden striker's performances when called upon, despite speculation about his future.

Should Arsenal locate a striker who they feel would be an upgrade on Gyokeres, they could allow him to move on, but that is not the case just yet.

"Viktor Gyokeres is going to be one to watch, I'm sure we'll keep on speaking about him," Brown told Football Insider.

"But from what I've heard, they're happy with how he's contributed this season and they're in no rush to force him out, they feel he can still play a massive role in their side.

"Even if he's not the first choice any more, he's still a good striker, and Arsenal aren't exactly blessed for goalscorers in that position.

"The only way I can see him leaving is if they identify somebody who would come in and do a better job, but as far as I can see, there isn't anybody who fits that mould.

"So unless that happens, they're going to be happy to keep Gyokeres, and they're happy with how he's been playing when called upon this season.".

Much of whether Gyokeres is allowed to leave the Emirates this summer will depend on the player's stance, and if he remains comfortable playing a lesser role under Arteta.

Having been pushed down the pecking order by the performances of Kai Havertz, there have been doubts over the striker's future, as he is keen to play more regularly.

Brown told Football Insider last month that Gyokeres could push to leave Arsenal if he is unhappy with his playing time, but for now, is working to get back into the side.

An impressive performance against Borussia Dortmund will have done his chances no harm, and a repeat of that display could ensure he remains at Arsenal long-term.

However, rival Premier League clubs are believed to be keeping tabs on Gyokeres' situation and could move to lure him away if they feel he could become available.
